observations: A jumble of used, rusty metal automotive parts piled on wooden shelves.
Visible items include engine mounts, brackets, pulleys, and cylindrical housings.
One black cylindrical part has handwritten white text, partially legible as "EKON..." and "moc...".
A watermark reads "POSTED ON KINGSLEY IBEN..." across the center.
Parts show corrosion, grime, and wear; no packaging or labels are visible.

identity.kind: used car engine mounts and brackets

claims.claim: For engine seatng and engines mouthing
claims.evidence: Photos show engine-like parts but cannot confirm fitment or purpose for a specific engine.

risks.risk: Individual parts may be cracked, bent, or worn out.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of each part, especially mounting rubber and bolt holes.

risks.risk: Compatibility with the buyer's vehicle is unknown.
risks.proof: Seller states vehicle make, model, year, and engine, or photos of part numbers.

risks.risk: Missing bolts, bushings, or small components.
risks.proof: Detailed shots showing all fasteners and rubber inserts present.

proof_requests: Clear individual photos of each part with any casting numbers.
Seller to confirm which car or engine these fit.
Video or photos showing rubber mounts are not perished or separated.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a lot of used engine mounts and brackets from the photos alone, so it can be priced at its worst case as used, fitment-unknown parts.
